items.evidence: 26.1.2's jar HAS DirtPathBlock (no PathBlock); the export chain is ['DirtPathBlock','Block']. But the 26.1.2 tree's classes.rs:208 (byte-identical to 26.1.1's) reads Path = "PathBlock" only — the "DirtPathBlock" alias 26.2's tree carries was dropped. The class resolves to plain Block, so every path arm is dead: survive (survive.rs:273), updateShape, scheduled tick (tick.rs:202, unconditional turn_to_base_block), placement. Dirt paths never revert to dirt when the block above becomes solid, and never revert on schedule. Vanilla 26.1.2 DirtPathBlock is byte-identical to 26.1.1's. Fix note: add "DirtPathBlock" to the Path alias (the 26.2 form), with the unit test 26.2's tree carries.
items.title: Dirt path never reverts: DirtPathBlock unmapped in classes.rs (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Two independent causes, either alone sufficient. (a) Class dispatch dead: 26.1.2 has no SpeleothemBlock (PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly, javap-verified fresh; export chain ['PointedDripstoneBlock','Block']), so the Class::Speleothem arms never fire: scheduled tick to spawn_falling_stalactite (tick.rs:248), random tick to growth (tick.rs:434), survive (survive.rs:307), updateShape (shapes.rs:728), placement (place.rs:1156). (b) Tag predicates dead: #speleothems is ABSENT from 26.1.2 data (block-tags.json and the client jar), so speleothem.rs:15, falling.rs:55, place.rs:1407, shapes.rs:1189 all fail; vanilla 26.1.2 uses hardcoded Blocks.POINTED_DRIPSTONE checks instead. Observable: dripstone never grows, stalactites never fall, can_survive defaults true (floating dripstone never pops), placement tip direction/thickness never computed. Fix note: dispatch on PointedDripstoneBlock directly and replace the #speleothems tag reads with a hardcoded pointed-dripstone check, matching vanilla 26.1.2's own form. While fixing, also fix the latent B5-G16: vanilla canGrow requires the fluid two blocks above to be WATER and a source (isSource(), javap-verified fresh); the port (speleothem.rs:104-107) checks only FluidKind::Water. Unobservable while growth is dead, so not minted separately.
items.title: Dripstone fully dead: no SpeleothemBlock class in 26.1.2 AND #speleothems tag absent (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 HAS bonemeal height gates (unlike 1.21.7), re-verified fresh by javap: SaplingBlock.isValidBonemealTarget = ServerLevel AND isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(getMinimumHeight)); AzaleaBlock = same + 2 and fluid above empty; MushroomBlock = feature exists AND AbstractHugeMushroomFeature AND HugeMushroomFeatureConfiguration AND isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(4 + foliageRadius)). The port's bonemeal_valid (bonemeal.rs:326-360) matches in form, but tree_minimum_height (growth.rs:446-453) reads json["trunk_placer"]["base_height"] at the JSON top level, while the stored feature JSON nests it under config — configured_json (worldgen/live.rs:234) returns the raw whole feature JSON. So it always returns 0 (vanilla base heights: oak 4, spruce 5, mangrove 2, azalea 4, birch 5, jungle 4, acacia 5, cherry 7, dark/pale oak 6; oak/spruce/azalea re-verified fresh in the 26.1.2 configured-feature JSON). Same nesting bug for mushrooms: the port reads json["foliage_radius"] top-level (bonemeal.rs:353) but it lives under config (brown = 3, red = 2, verified fresh); the port always uses 2 — red correct by luck, brown's gate is pos.y+6 instead of pos.y+7. isBonemealSuccess (sapling/azalea 0.45, mushroom/fungus 0.4) matches vanilla exactly. Fix note: read config.trunk_placer.base_height and config.foliage_radius (or make configured_json return the config object). The opposite direction (too strict) is B5-G29 — both directions are live at once in 26.1.2.
items.title: Bonemeal validity too permissive at the build ceiling: sapling/azalea/mushroom height gates read the wrong JSON level (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 ChorusFlowerBlock.randomTick proceeds when above.y <= getMaxY() (320) — bytecode if_icmple 28, re-verified fresh. The port (tick.rs:1430, chorus_flower_random_tick, file byte-identical to 26.1.1's) returns early when above_pos.y > max_y() - 1, i.e. above.y >= 320. A flower at pos.y == 319: vanilla still ages/branches (horizontal targets at y=319 are in-bounds); the port returns early and the flower stays forever young. The rest of the chorus logic matches exactly (age < 5, support/pillar logic, height < 2 || height <= rand(5 or 4), grow-up with allNeighborsEmpty + empty at +2, branch attempts rand(4) + pillar?1:0, events 1033/1034, age-5 death).
items.title: Chorus flower never ticks at the build ceiling (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: NEVER EXISTED — a correction to the 26.1, 26.1.1 and 26.2 records. The 26.1.1 item claimed vanilla BellBlock.isProperHit requires click_y > 0.8123999834060669 and the port's click_y <= 0.8124f32 (redstone.rs:1442) was inverted. Fresh 26.1.2 evidence, three ways: (1) bytecode — dload_3; ldc2_w 0.8123999834060669d; dcmpl; ifle 20; 18: iconst_0; ireturn; 20: <attachment switch> — ifle branches to the only true-returning path exactly when clickY <= 0.8124; a click above 0.8124 falls through to return false; (2) Vineflower 1.12.0 decompilation gives the source form verbatim: if (clickedDirection.getAxis() != Axis.Y && !(clickY > 0.8124F)) — the earlier runs dropped the negation when reading the branch; (3) physical sense — the bell body tops out at y = 13/16 = 0.8125 (BELL_SHAPE), the mount column is 13.0-16.0, so clicking at y <= 0.8124 hits the bell body. The port implements vanilla's gate exactly, including the value (f64::from(0.8124f32) is exactly the jar's double constant) and the within-block Y at the callers (interact.rs:424, mod.rs:1363). BellBlock is byte-identical across the 26.1/26.1.1/26.1.2 jars and the port code is byte-identical across the three trees, so the item never existed in any of the three runs. The bell check is a PASS in 26.1.2. No fix needed — there is nothing to fix. The 26.1 and 26.1.1 ledgers carry G18 as a live minor gap and need this correction.
items.title: Bell isProperHit height comparison: the port was correct all along (NEVER EXISTED — 26.2/26.1/26.1.1 misread)

items.evidence: The port reads #convertible_to_mud (with 'i') in four places: data.rs:460 (tag table), horizon-client/src/game/potions.rs:710 (water bottle use), horizon-client/src/game/remote.rs:8658, horizon-client/src/game/dispenser.rs:2245 (dispenser water bottle). 26.1.2's tag is #convertable_to_mud (with 'a') — verified three ways: BlockTags.CONVERTABLE_TO_MUD in the jar, data/minecraft/tags/block/convertable_to_mud.json in the client jar (dirt, coarse_dirt, rooted_dirt — verified fresh in the prepared block-tags.json), and vanilla PotionItem.useOn checks it (bytecode offset 57, re-verified fresh). The port's tag read returns nothing, so the mud conversion never fires. 26.2's tree uses the correct 'a' spelling; the 26.1.2 port wrongly took the 26.3 spelling (convertable_to_mud appears nowhere in the data.rs tag table). items.title: Water bottle on dirt never makes mud: port reads #convertible_to_mud, 26.1.2's tag is #convertable_to_mud (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: The port's portal_frame() (portal.rs:40-44, file byte-identical to 26.1.1's) reads #nether_portal_frame, which is ABSENT from 26.1.2 data (verified in block-tags.json; no synthesis anywhere in the tree) — always false. Vanilla 26.1.2 PortalShape.FRAME is hardcoded state.is(Blocks.OBSIDIAN) (lambda$static$0 in PortalShape, re-verified fresh; the class lives at net.minecraft.world.level.portal.PortalShape). Consequence: find_portal_shape (portal.rs:67) always returns width/height 0, find_empty_portal_shape (portal.rs:131) always returns None, and hooks.rs:588-597 base_fire_on_place never creates portal blocks — no nether portal can ever be created in the 26.1.2 port. 26.2's tree correctly hardcoded obsidian. items.title: No nether portal can ever be created: portal_frame reads the absent #nether_portal_frame tag (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: The port's motion_blocking_top (weather.rs:41-59, file byte-identical to 26.1.1's) reads #blocks_motion_in_heightmap, which is ABSENT from 26.1.2 data (verified in block-tags.json; no synthesis anywhere in the tree) — only fluids count as motion-blocking. Vanilla 26.1.2 Heightmap.MATERIAL_MOTION_BLOCKING is a method reference to BlockStateBase.blocksMotion() (bootstrap method 1 in Heightmap, re-verified fresh with javap -v). Consequence: precipitation_info computes top = min_y in fluidless columns — snow never accumulates on land and ice never forms except on water. The same wrong top also feeds is_raining_at (weather.rs:127), lightning strike height (lightning.rs:199), and portal-travel spawn height (portal_travel.rs:506). 26.2's tree correctly used per-state blocksMotion(). Same-root-cause site: feature_world.rs:350-360 also reads #blocks_motion_in_heightmap / #blocks_motion_in_heightmap_no_leaves (both tags absent), so feature-placement heightmaps (OceanFloor, MotionBlocking, MotionBlockingNoLeaves) are broken the same way; recorded here as an additional site of this item. Fix note: replace the tag reads with the per-state blocksMotion() value from the prepared data (26.2's form), or synthesise the tag at prepare time from it.
items.title: Snow never accumulates on land, ice never forms except on water: motion_blocking_top reads the absent #blocks_motion_in_heightmap tag (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 ComposterBlock composts by a static chance table: COMPOSTABLES (Object2FloatMap<ItemLike>, 115 entries) and addItem (bytecode read fresh): level 0 + chance > 0 adds a layer with NO roll; above level 0 it adds one when the level random rolls under the chance (nextDouble() < chance). The 26.1 tree implemented exactly this (compost_chance, 115/115 exact). The 26.1.2 tree carries the 26.1.1 tree's 26.3 form: horizon-items/src/items.rs:1015 populates the item's compostable field ONLY from the minecraft:compostable component — and ZERO of the 1,506 items in the prepared 26.1.2 items.json carry that component (26.1.2 vanilla has no compostable component; 26.3 added it). compost_chance does not exist anywhere in the 26.1.2 tree (grep: zero hits). game/composter.rs:29-38 therefore returns None for every item: use_composter returns false (no hand composting), composter_container_insert returns the stack untouched (no hopper composting), villager_insert_item returns early (no villager composting), composter_takes is false for every held item. The level side (level/interact.rs:559-633) lost composter_add_item entirely: composter_insert/composter_layer now take a layers count directly, so the level-0-always-adds rule and the chance roll exist nowhere in the tree. Observable: no item can ever be composted in the 26.1.2 port by any path. (The level-7 to 8 tick itself still functions if a composter reaches level 7 by command; the insertion path is what is dead.) Fix note: restore the 26.1 form — the compost_chance table plus composter_add_item with the level-0 rule.
items.title: Composter completely dead: the port reads the minecraft:compostable component no 26.1.2 item carries (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 IceBlock.playerDestroy (bytecode read fresh, offsets 52-86): unless the tool prevents melting or water evaporates, if the block below blocksMotion() OR is liquid, the position becomes water (setBlockAndUpdate(meltsInto())). items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 schedules a tripwire re-check tick 10 ONLY while pressed: TripWireBlock's single scheduleTick is bipush 10 gated on the pressed flag (offsets 124-141, fresh javap), and TripWireHookBlock has exactly ONE scheduleTick in the whole class — the 10-tick attached-circuit re-check inside calculateState (offset 281). There is no 1-tick unpress re-check anywhere in either class. The 26.1 tree matched this, with a comment stating the pressed-to-unpressed immediate re-check is 26.2-only. items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 EyeblossomBlock.tryChangingState iterates the 7x5x7 neighbour box with BlockPos.betweenClosed (offset 99, fresh javap) — x innermost, then y, then z — and each matching neighbour draws its delay from nextIntBetweenInclusive(dist*5, dist*10) in that scan order. The 26.1 tree matched this with between_closed (plus a unit test pinning the order). The 26.1.2 tree replaced it with box_scan_order (timeline.rs:9-23, the 26.3 findBlocksIn order: sections by x, z, y; blocks by y, z, x), used by eyeblossom_tick (timeline.rs:92). Vanilla 26.1.2 has no blockscan package at all (0 jar entries). Observable: the per-neighbour random draws are assigned in a different order, so the cascade delays differ from vanilla for the same seed (the open/close windows themselves still match: (12600..23401)). Fix note: restore between_closed and its test, the 26.1 form.
items.title: Eyeblossom neighbour cascade scans in 26.3 section order instead of betweenClosed order (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 BedBlock.useWithoutItem (bytecode read fresh): client returns SUCCESS_SERVER; if part != HEAD, redirect to the head and require only that the head is this bed (else CONSUME); a HEAD click needs no foot check at all — it proceeds straight to the BED_RULE path (sleep or explode). The 26.1 tree matched this. The 26.1.2 tree's Class::AbstractBed arm (interact.rs:367-384) implements the 26.3 pair check: it requires the block at the other half's position to be this bed with the opposite part, else returns Consume. Observable: clicking the head of a bed whose foot was destroyed (or replaced) sleeps in vanilla 26.1.2 but does nothing in the port; the foot-click path is unaffected (both forms Consume when the head is missing). Fix note: restore the 26.1 form (foot redirects to head, head needs no foot check). Note: the 26.1.2 tree's sleep_height change in game/beds.rs (shape-top form) is NOT a defect — for every 26.1.2 bed the shape top is 9/16 = 0.5625 and pos_to_bed adds 0.125, giving exactly vanilla's flat 0.6875 (LivingEntity.setPosToBed, javap-verified fresh); the straw-bed branch is dead (no straw_bed in the 26.1.2 export).
items.title: Bed use requires the other half: a head click with no foot returns Consume instead of sleeping (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 SaplingBlock.isValidBonemealTarget is ONLY the height check (ServerLevel AND isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(getMinimumHeight)), javap-verified fresh) — there is no canGrow method on 26.1.2's TreeGrower at all. The 26.1 tree matched this, with a comment noting canGrow (the 2x2 requirement for a mega-only grower) is 26.3-only, so a lone dark oak sapling takes the meal (and consumes it 45% of the time with no growth). The 26.1.2 tree's bonemeal_valid (bonemeal.rs:335) adds !self.tree_can_grow(g, pos, state) — tree_can_grow (growth.rs:425-444) returns false for a mega-only grower (dark oak, pale oak — empty trees list, non-empty mega_trees) with no 2x2 square. Observable: bonemeal on a lone dark/pale oak sapling is refused outright in the port; vanilla 26.1.2 accepts it (and the 0.45 success roll consumes the meal with no tree). The gate also draws random (weighted on both lists) on EVERY sapling/azalea validity check, shifting the RNG stream where vanilla draws nothing. The 26.1.2 tree's own growth_tests.rs asserts the refusal (lone_dark_oak_sapling_cannot_grow) where the 26.1 test asserted the meal is taken. Fix note: delete the tree_can_grow gate, restoring the 26.1 form. The opposite direction (too permissive at the ceiling) is the reproduced B5-G15 — both directions are live at once.
items.title: Bonemeal validity too strict: the 26.3 canGrow gate refuses lone dark/pale oak saplings (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1 — 1.21.7 G15's original form)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 TreeGrower (bytecode + fields read fresh) is the secondary-chance form: 10 growers (oak, spruce, mangrove, azalea, birch, jungle, acacia, cherry, dark oak, pale oak — NO poplar), secondaryChance float, megaTree/secondaryMegaTree/tree/secondaryTree/flowers/secondaryFlowers optionals. getConfiguredFeature draws ONE nextFloat() unconditionally (even at chance 0) against secondaryChance; getConfiguredMegaFeature draws only when a secondary mega tree exists (spruce only). The 26.1 tree implemented exactly this (with three unit tests pinning the draw counts). The 26.1.2 tree carries the 26.1.1 tree's 26.3 weighted-list form (growth.rs:145-269): trees/mega_trees/flower_trees weight lists plus weighted() (growth.rs:249-264, next_int_bound(total)), a shortest field, and a poplar grower (dead — no poplar_sapling in the 26.1.2 export). Observable: the probabilities coincide (oak fancy 10%, mangrove tall 85%, spruce mega 50/50) but the draw type (nextInt vs nextFloat) and draw count differ — jungle's mega draw happens in the port (total 1) where vanilla draws nothing, and every single-tree grower draws nextInt(1) where vanilla draws a float — so the chosen tree (fancy vs regular oak, tall vs short mangrove, mega spruce vs mega pine) and the RNG stream after it diverge from vanilla for the same seed. Fix note: restore the 26.1 secondary-chance form and its tests.
items.title: TreeGrower rewritten in the 26.3 weighted-list form: tree selection diverges from vanilla's secondary-chance draws (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1)

items.title: Mega sapling growth leaves water where vanilla 26.1.2 leaves air (REPRODUCES from 26.1.1 — 1.21.7 G14's form, mega path)
